newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BOB WATSON IS FIRST BLACK GM TO WIN SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BOB WATSON IS FIRST BLACK GM TO WIN SERIES.

text.p: New York Yankees General Manager Bob Watson, the first black GM to win a World Series, noted that next year will mark a half-century since Jackie Robionson broke the major-league colour barrier.

Asked what he was especially proud of, Watson said: "That I'm sitting here as the only minority vice president of baseball operations, with the 50th anniversary of Jackie Robinson coming next year, that I am the principal architect of a championship club.
"I hope that other minorities are given this opportunity."
Watson has had his problems with Yankee owner George Steinbrenner, who gave a vote of confidence to manager Joe Torre when the team was in a late-season slump but refused to do the same for Watson.

Steinbrenner, Watson has said, also threatened to fire him unless he managed to undo a trade in which the Yankees appeared to have received damaged goods from the Milwaukee Brewers -- although one player in the deal, Australian reliever Graeme Lloyd, was perfect in the post-season for New York.
"You can say what you want about Mr Steinbrenner," Watson said. "He wants to win as much as anybody."
Watson would not say he was "vindicated" by the victory.
"Let me put it this way," he said. "The way I feel right now is very, very good.

"I was part of a group of men that put together what is now the world championship team. There were a number of people who go into making trades, but I am held accountable. Vindicated? I don't think that's the word I want to use. I feel really good right now.
"To be honest, what I want now is to ride down 5th Avenue in a ticker-tape parade. I've never been in one of those before."
He will get his parade on Tuesday.
